data.raw_text:
🌎 The Earthquake 01 July 2025

Looking at the latest USGS seismic map, there is a clear concentration of earthquake activity on the eastern side of the Pacific Plate from Alaska down to South America. This pressure release on the U.S. side of the Ring of Fire raises a valid concern.

🗾 Could Japan and the western Pacific be next?

Japan sits on a major subduction zone where the Pacific Plate dives beneath the Eurasian Plate. Historically, when one side of the plate boundary relieves stress, the opposing side often builds it. If the seismic quiet in Japan continues while the opposite edge is this active, it might only be a matter of time before a significant shift occurs.

While no one can predict earthquakes with certainty patterns and pressure transfer are real.

🤯 Growing anxiety by 私が見た未来

“The Future I Saw" (私が見た未来, Watashi ga Mita Mirai) is a manga by Ryo Tatsuki

After the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami, when it was found that the cover of the book had apparently predicted a disaster occurring in March 2011.

The 2021 reprint, “The Future I Saw (Complete Version),” revived popularity warned of a "real disaster" on 5th July 2025, a crack will open up under the seabed between Japan and the Philippines, sending ashore waves three times as tall as those from the Tohoku earthquake.

#Earthquake #Japan #TheFutureISaw #USGS #私が見た未来 #05July2025
